lesson.title: Procedure 410 – LIMITING SENSITIVE/DELICATE ANNOUNCEMENTS
lesson.topic: Radio Discipline – Avoiding Sensational Labels While Preserving Officer Safety
objectives: Explain why Procedure 410 limits sensitive/delicate announcements and how media response can disrupt operations.
Identify example labels that should be avoided over the radio.
Apply when perpetrator full name and date of birth must be transmitted over the air (and the listed qualifiers/exceptions).
Apply restrictions (juveniles; sexual assault family/household) and use alternate methods when appropriate.
Apply supervisor notification and supervisory control requirements for sensitive cases.

questions.stem: Procedure 410 SCOPE: Why should dispatchers avoid unnecessary details, descriptions, and names on the radio?

choices.text: Because they can cause an extreme response by the news media
Because they replace the need for unit response

questions.solution: The SCOPE explains unnecessary details/descriptions/names can cause an extreme news media response.
questions.hints: Think: it’s about publicity and media reaction, not safety.

source.coverage: Balance safety details with avoiding unnecessary details/names that drive media response

questions.stem: Procedure 410 PURPOSE: What can happen when an event is dispatched and labeled with a highly publicized name?

choices.text: It automatically upgrades the job type
It reduces the need for detective follow-up
It can cause a tremendous response by the news media and disrupt police operations/investigations

questions.solution: The PURPOSE explains that publicized labels trigger heavy media response and severe disruption to operations and detective investigations.

questions.solution: RADIO (2) instructs dispatchers to immediately notify the radio supervisor of sensitive cases to be dispatched.
